title: Test expert gradients against matched numerical proposals
hypothesis: Assembly expert gradients can coordinate existing placement parameters more efficiently than independent numerical proposals when checkpoints are selected by rollout success.

prediction.against: baseline: five-candidate numerical search from each frozen D-020 assembly incumbent
prediction.rationale: A 10-point gain on fresh cases would show useful expert-guided parameter proposals beyond an equally rollout-selected numerical trajectory.

code_changes: scripts/compare_generation_modes.py (--assembly-study expert-fit-vs-numerical: demo audit, gradient feasibility check, rollout-selected imitation checkpoints vs five numerical candidates, both winners on 30 screen cases)

falsified_by: The upper paired confidence bound for fitted-minus-numerical success is below 0.10. An interval including zero is inconclusive; the resolving measurement is the same frozen winners' paired success on another fresh development manifest, not their imitation losses.

approval.note: approved by advisor gpt-6.1-sol (consult call_00043, 'revise' with changes applied) under the user's 2026-10-22 session delegation

controls.note: control is the five-candidate numerical search from the same frozen starting vector, rollout-selected on the same probe; the metric is already fitted minus numerical

result.notes: Frozen D-020 assembly structures; fresh 50-case development pool (seed 3410): expert demonstrations on cases 40-49 (10/10 succeeded), probe 0-4, screen 10-39. Gradient reached the placement parameters of both structures (feasible without changing their code). Imitation of the assembly expert (deterministic MSE, checkpoints 0/100/300/600/1000, rollout-selected) never produced a probe success and steadily lowered goal progress (0.23 at step 0 to 0.13-0.18), so step 0 was kept for both structures; the five numerical candidates also never succeeded. Fitted minus numerical on the 30 screen cases: +0.000 [0, 0] (both 0.00). Upper bound below the predicted +0.10: refuted. Consistent with push-v2's finding that imitating the expert's actions does not transfer to these structures. 230 episodes, 0 LLM calls.

verdicts.reasoning: Fitted minus numerical is +0.000 [0, 0]; both arms score 0.00 on the 30 screen cases, below the predicted +0.10. With reliable demonstrations (10/10) and gradients reaching the placement parameters, imitation of the expert still never produced a probe success and reduced goal progress at every checkpoint, so rollout selection kept step 0. Expert gradients do not coordinate these structures' placement parameters.
verdicts.next_experiment: Parameter-level methods (search, imitation) cannot seat the nut with these two structures; the D-021 handoff shows the needed behaviour exists in the expert. Next: structural changes aimed at the placement phase (e.g. an LLM structural edit with handoff evidence, or more independent structures per R-027).

verdicts.reasoning: The named numerical-search control was measured, and fitted-minus-numerical paired success was 0.000 with a reported 95% interval of [0.000, 0.000] [logs/assembly_fitting_s3410/summary.json]. Its upper bound is below the predicted +0.10, meeting the approved falsification criterion; the tie does not establish any difference between methods [logs/assembly_fitting_s3410/summary.json]. Both structures selected the unfitted checkpoint, so this result refutes the specified improvement for this protocol, not expert-gradient fitting in general [logs/assembly_fitting_s3410/summary.json]. The experiment consumed 230 simulator episodes and zero LLM calls [logs/assembly_fitting_s3410/summary.json].
